Stir the flour, oats, sugar, salt, and instant yeast together in a roomy bowl, or
the bowl of a stand mixer. Warm the milk, water, and oil in a small pan, a
safe jug, until they reach 120°F to 130°F. Stir the mixture well before
you trust the reading; the bottom is always hotter. If you don’t own a ther-
mometer, aim for a little warmer than a hot bath, but never so hot that it
hurts to keep a finger in it.

Add the warm liquid to the dry mix in the bowl. Using a wooden spoon,
or stand mixer with paddle attachment, mix hard for 2 minutes; the dough
should look glossy and loose. If you are mixing by hand, keep at it
for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the dough pulls away in sticky strands.

Lightly oil an 8%" X 4%" loaf tin, and dust the base and sides with rolled oats.
Spoon the loose dough into the tin, smoothing the top with a wet hand.

Cover the tin, and let the dough rise until it’s just peeking above the rim of the
tin. When you crouch down to the counter, you should sce a soft dome,
but it shouldn’t be more than, say, %~ over the rim. Allow around 50 minutes
to 1 hour, depending how warm your kitchen is and whether the liquid was
hot enough. While the dough is rising, preheat the oven to 375°F.

Take off the cover, and bake the loaf fo
r 30 to 35 minutes, until it’s a deep gold

and its interior temperature is 190°E

Pull the loaf from the oven, and after 10
minutes, slide it out of the tin onto a

es,
rack. Let the loaf go completely cold be
fore slicing.
